problem: A worse valid checkpoint replaced the rollback coordinates even when it did not replace the selected best candidate. A later invalid block therefore restarted from a poorer fit and lost the useful bird-eye boundary.
change: Keep the rollback coordinates with the best physically valid candidate under the existing selection/preference comparator. Worse valid checkpoints still continue exploration. Invalid states still trigger rollback and the same rate reduction.
controls: No changes to probabilities, crop, original-image or feature thresholds, gradients, paper tolerances, routing budget, or count portfolio.
visualReview: Both exported bird renders inspected: small enclosed eye retained without enlargement; torso opening preserved. Existing thin contact seams and frame irregularities remain.

regressionCoverage.analytic: Both boundary and mask selection tests fail before the change at the resumed-coordinate assertion and pass after. They use actual gradients and an injected uncertain audit, compare against an independent restart, and require exploration through worse valid checkpoints.
regressionCoverage.photographic: Existing x+1 bird tests enforce independent 400/800-pixel errors below 2.7%, eye retention at least 90%, eye IoU above 0.85, closed eye, geometry/paper, Stop and timing requirements.

limitations: The two timed replays are the same photograph, not independent motifs.
No general speed claim or corpus-wide quality guarantee follows from this result.
Gift/Viking and earlier crop/coverage issues remain separate.
